concepts.def: The Reichstag Fire Decree, Enabling Act, banning of parties and the Night of the Long Knives made Hitler Führer of a one-party state by 1934.
The SS and Gestapo, helped by informers and concentration camps, crushed opposition, while courts and judges were brought under Nazi control.
Goebbels's ministry controlled newspapers, cheap 'people's receiver' radios, film and mass rallies such as Nuremberg to spread the Hitler myth.
The Hitler Youth and League of German Maidens trained boys for war and girls for motherhood, while school subjects were rewritten around race and loyalty.
Persecution escalated from the 1933 boycott through the Nuremberg Laws of 1935 and Kristallnacht in 1938 to ghettos and the Holocaust during the war.
War brought rationing, bombing and total mobilisation, and resistance grew from groups like the White Rose to the July 1944 bomb plot.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Living Under Nazi Rule 1933-1945 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Living Under Nazi Rule 1933-1945 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Living Under Nazi Rule 1933-1945.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What did the Nuremberg Laws of 1935 do?
options: Stripped Jews of citizenship and banned marriage between Jews and other Germans
Banned Jews from emigrating from Germany
Set up the first concentration camp at Dachau
Forced all German Jews into ghettos

mcqs.q: What was the role of the Gestapo?
options: A secret state police that investigated opposition, relying heavily on public denunciations
Hitler's personal bodyguard regiment
The Nazi youth organisation
The ministry responsible for propaganda

mcqs.q: Which organisation did the Nazis use to indoctrinate boys?
options: The Hitler Youth
The Edelweiss Pirates
The White Rose
The Freikorps

mcqs.q: What happened on Kristallnacht in November 1938?
options: Nazi-organised attacks destroyed synagogues and Jewish shops, and around 30,000 Jewish men were sent to camps
Jewish citizenship was restored by court order
The first Allied bombing raid hit Berlin
Hitler survived an assassination attempt

mcqs.q: Did the Gestapo have agents watching every German?
options: No - the Gestapo was a relatively small organisation that depended heavily on tip-offs and denunciations from ordinary Germans.
The Hitler Youth was banned by the Nazis in 1936.
The Gestapo had an agent on every street corner watching everyone.
The Gestapo was the German army's tank division.

mcqs.q: Did all young Germans enthusiastically support the Hitler Youth?
options: Every young German was a devoted Nazi through the Hitler Youth.
No - membership became effectively compulsory by 1939, and groups such as the Edelweiss Pirates and Swing Youth rejected its discipline and culture.
The Hitler Youth was banned by the Nazis in 1936.
Persecution of the Jews only began after the war started in 1939.

mcqs.q: Could ordinary Germans have been unaware that Jews were being persecuted?
options: The Gestapo was the German army's tank division.
Ordinary Germans could not have known about any persecution of the Jews.
No - the 1933 boycott, the Nuremberg Laws and Kristallnacht were public and publicised, although knowledge of the wartime death camps varied.
Persecution of the Jews only began after the war started in 1939.
